stem:
A student investigates the discharge of a capacitor in the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The student closes the switch and charges the capacitor.

The switch is opened and a stop-watch is started. The capacitor discharges through the two resistors of resistance *R*₁ and *R*₂ connected between P and Q. At a fixed time *t* the potential difference *V* across the capacitor is measured.

The experiment is repeated for different values of *R*₁ and *R*₂.

It is suggested that *V*, *R*₁ and *R*₂ are related by the equation

ln(*V*/*E*) = −*t*/[*C*(*R*₁ + *R*₂)]

where *E* is the electromotive force (e.m.f.) of the battery and *C* is the capacitance of the capacitor.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of ln *V* on the *y*-axis against 1/(*R*₁ + *R*₂) on the *x*-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and *y*-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *R*₁, *R*₂, *V* and ln *V* are given in Table 2.1.

Each resistance value has a percentage uncertainty of ±5%.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate and record values of (*R*₁ + *R*₂)/kΩ and 1/(*R*₁ + *R*₂)/10⁻⁶ Ω⁻¹ in Table 2.1.

Include the absolute uncertainties in (*R*₁ + *R*₂) and 1/(*R*₁ + *R*₂).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of ln (*V*/V) against 1/(*R*₁ + *R*₂)/10⁻⁶ Ω⁻¹.

Include error bars for 1/(*R*₁ + *R*₂).

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Both lines should be clearly labelled.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the *y*-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *C* and *E*. Include appropriate units.

Data: *t* = (60 ± 1) s

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: The experiment is repeated using the same capacitor. Determine the value of (*R*₁ + *R*₂) that would give a value of *V* of 5.0 V at time *t* = 60 s.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: Circuit diagram showing a battery and switch connected to a capacitor, with two resistors R₁ and R₂ between P and Q and a voltmeter across the capacitor.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: Table of resistance values, reciprocal resistance-sum, voltage and ln(V/V), with blank cells for calculated values.
Blank graph grid with ln(V/V) on the vertical axis and 1/(R₁ + R₂)/10⁻⁶ Ω⁻¹ on the horizontal axis.
